claims.text: The initial substrate is a clean, pre-treated Cu matrix ready for deposition.
A Cu-enriched HEA can be used as a graded interlayer between a Cu matrix and a refractory HEA coating.
Introducing the Cu-rich graded interlayer will improve adhesion of the refractory HEA coating to Cu.
The graded interlayer will reduce lattice mismatch between Cu and the refractory HEA coating.
The graded interlayer will reduce differences in thermal expansion between Cu and the refractory HEA coating.
Improved interfacial adhesion will enhance wear resistance and surface protection.
DC-magnetron sputtering under suitable conditions can produce the proposed Cu-rich graded interlayer and promote interdiffusion.
Controlled deposition and annealing can facilitate a gradual compositional transition across the interface.
A compositional gradient in the interlayer produces a corresponding structural transition.
The graded transition minimizes abrupt changes in lattice parameters across the Cu-to-RHEA interface.
The graded transition minimizes abrupt changes in thermal expansion coefficients across the Cu-to-RHEA interface.
Gradually transitioning from Cu to the refractory HEA reduces interfacial stresses.
Gradually transitioning from Cu to the refractory HEA reduces bonding discontinuities.
Reducing interfacial stresses and bonding discontinuities helps prevent coating delamination under mechanical and thermal loads.
A refractory HEA can provide high wear resistance.
The proposed interlayer will increase quantitative coating adhesion strength and reduce delamination during wear testing.
Direct deposition of a refractory HEA coating onto Cu typically gives poor adhesion because of lattice and thermal-expansion mismatch.
Extreme oxidizing environments or very high thermal gradients may require further optimization of the proposed coating system.
